verdicts.evidence:
This row also covers F-sol-F1-1, reported separately; its SIGTERM and SIGHUP entry-window claims are covered below. Method: a private scratch copy with a temporary HOME and TMPDIR and a stand-in `claude` first on PATH that prints the trust-dialog text, so the probe ends its observation by itself. A driver used sys.settrace; at the target line event it called os.kill(getpid, sig), and the probe's leave() raised from that point.

Results on python3 (3.13.15):
- No injection: alert and push both gave exit 2, client alive false, 0 directories left, printed "raw payload directory removed: True".
- SIGHUP at alert_probe.py:556 or push_notification_probe.py:579: {"exit": 129, "client_alive_after_probe_exit": true, "private_dirs_left": 0, "printed": ["raw payload directory removed: True"]}.
- SIGHUP at 557 or 580, inside the `with`: exit 129, client alive false. The deferral works once the mask is up.
- SIGTERM at 435 or 441: {"exit": 143, "private_dirs_left": 1, "private_files_left": ["events.log"], printed "raw payload directory removed: False"}.
- SIGTERM at 436 or 442, inside the `with`: exit -15, 0 directories left.

On /usr/bin/python3.12 (3.12.3) all four leak cases reproduced the same way (129 with the client alive; 143 with events.log left).

Severity reasoning:
- Only the first signal can hit the window. With SIGTERM sent inside the spawn wrapper plus SIGHUP at line 556 or 579, the driver printed "line 556: the handler returned without raising" (SIG_IGN had already been set), and the run gave exit 143 with the client gone.
- The window is at most about 4 µs. A timeit of deferred_signals().__enter__ plus one extra unmask call gave 4.12e-06 s.
- It is reachable only on the normal-exit path or a non-signal exception path.
- The directory comes from mkdtemp (mode 0700) in the user's own TMPDIR.
- What the real client does when the pty master closes is unverified: no real session was run.

The claim this breaks is the with_private_dir docstring (alert_probe.py:426-428, push_notification_probe.py:432-434): "the cleanup runs with the signals deferred until it is done, so none of them can cut it short". That makes this wrong edge behavior with an overstated claim: medium, not high.
verdicts.fix_assessment: The direction is right and sufficient: latch the signal instead of raising asynchronously, and act on it at safe points. It also covers the spawn-window defects in F-ultra-F1-2. Side effects: the observation loop and the prompt-typing loop must check the latch. With a non-raising handler, select() is retried on EINTR (PEP 475), so the stop is delayed by up to the 0.2 s select timeout. The final exit must come after both finally blocks. The proposed deterministic tests work: the line-trace injections at the cleanup entries used here tell a leaking probe from a fixed one. The existing cleanup_phase_case cannot, because it injects inside rmtree, after the mask is up.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In both probes, make leave() record only the first signal and never raise. Check that record in the observation loop and right after the spawn, and raise SystemExit(128+signal) only after both cleanups have finished. Add line-trace cases at alert 556/435 and push 579/441 that require the client to be gone and the directory removed.
verdicts.adjacent: Verified, same root cause: the directory exists before its protection. with_private_dir creates it (alert_probe.py:429, push_notification_probe.py:435) before the handlers are installed (431 / 437). SIGTERM injected at line 431 or 437 gave {"exit": -15, "private_dirs_left": 1, "private_files_left": []}: an empty alert-probe-* directory is left behind, with no payload file yet.

verdicts.evidence:
This row also covers F-sol-F1-2 (sub-claim a), and F-sol-F1-3, F-ultra-F3-3 and F-sol-F3-3 (sub-claim b), all reported separately.

(a) Signal lost between the two stores ("cancellation is lost, the client starts"). This happens only under instrumentation.
- With an opcode trace on python3 (3.13.15), a signal delivered before the second store at alert:472 or push:483 printed "SPAWN before={'active': True, 'signal': None}" and then "handler returned: SPAWN after={'active': True, 'signal': 15}", followed by "main returned 2", so the exit was 2, not 143. The same injection never fired under 3.12.3 in my driver, so this sub-claim is not verified on 3.12.
- It cannot happen without tracing. dis of line 472 on both 3.13.15 and 3.12.3 gives "LOAD_CONST UNPACK_SEQUENCE LOAD_GLOBAL LOAD_CONST STORE_SUBSCR LOAD_GLOBAL LOAD_CONST STORE_SUBSCR": nothing between the two stores lets the interpreter stop to run a signal handler.
- An untraced storm of SIGALRM every 20 µs, using the same statement shape, never found the handler between the stores: 3.13.15 {'total': 66167, 'between_the_stores': 0}, 3.12.3 {'total': 88118, 'between_the_stores': 0}.
- The Python 3.13 signal docs (fetched today) say an exception from a handler "may be raised after any bytecode instruction". So the store order is a latent defect against the documented contract, not reachable behavior today.

(b) Reachable: two different signals while the client is being created. The wrapper sent SIGTERM then SIGINT. Both probes, on 3.13.15 and 3.12.3, printed "SystemExit(130) left main; SPAWN={'active': False, 'signal': 2}", exit 130, with the client gone and 0 directories left. Only the exit status is wrong.

(c) SIGTERM inside the spawn, then SIGHUP at line 479 or 490 (line trace): exit 129 while SPAWN held 15. Untraced, the next check after the flag clears is the entry of the leave() call on line 480 (dis: LOAD_GLOBAL LOAD_CONST BINARY_SUBSCR POP_JUMP_IF_NONE LOAD_GLOBAL LOAD_GLOBAL LOAD_CONST BINARY_SUBSCR CALL). So this is real but the window is tiny.

(d) Removing only the first-signal-wins loop still passes all six packaged cases (see F-sol-F1-4).

Medium rests on (b) and (c), which break the leave() docstring (alert 406, push 412: "The first signal wins (later ones are ignored)") and decision record line 385 ("The first signal now wins"). It does not endorse the lost-cancellation headline.
verdicts.fix_assessment: Sufficient and safe. Clearing the signal before setting the flag closes (a) against the documented contract. Letting leave() store only the first signal, and exit with that stored value, closes (b) and (c). Sharing one cancellation record with the F-ultra-F1-1 repair is cleaner still. The reviewer is right that the tests must mix signal kinds: repeating the same signal cannot show which one won.
verdicts.smallest_repair:
In both probes:
- Split lines 472 and 483 into `SPAWN["signal"] = None` followed by `SPAWN["active"] = True`.
- In leave(), store the signal only when none is stored, and raise SystemExit with the stored signal when there is one.

Add a spawn-wrapper case that sends SIGTERM then SIGINT and requires exit 143.

verdicts.evidence:
Method: client_boundary_case ran on scratch variants of each probe, with blocked_mask wrapped to record the process state, its argv and its blocked-signal mask (SigBlk) at each sample. HOME was a temporary directory.

With the stand-in changed to `exec sleep 0`, the case passed with the spawn guard as shipped and also with the guard disabled (the packaged mutant's replacement). Both probes, all four combinations, returned ok true: "stand-in client ran True with signal mask 0000000000000000, probe exit 143 (expected 143), private directory left False, stand-in client still alive False". The mask samples were [["Z", [""], "0000000000000000"]], taken from a zombie. So the reviewer's reproduction holds: the check at alert_probe.py:252 / push_notification_probe.py:254 never requires a live, correctly identified client.

The deciding result is the stand-in as shipped with the guard disabled: ok false, "... stand-in client still alive True", mask sample ["S", ["sleep", "313791289"], "0000000000000000"]. It fails on both probes. As shipped, with the guard on, the case passes with the mask sampled from the live `sleep <unique>`. The control therefore works as shipped.

The stand-in is shared: signal_case uses the same `sleep` stand-in, and in the same selftest its liveness check (stand_in_alive) and its "never starts" negative control would catch a stand-in that exits early. The case would pass vacuously only if client_boundary_case itself changed. That makes this a missing precondition (hygiene), not a control that cannot fail: low.
verdicts.fix_assessment: Sufficient and safe. The readiness check belongs where the mask is sampled (the parent loop at lines 231-234 / 233-236): accept a sample only while the recorded PID is non-zombie and is exactly `sleep <unique>`, as signal_case's stand_in_alive does. The negative control (a stand-in that publishes its PID and exits) must be rejected by both the shipped and the guard-disabled variants.
verdicts.smallest_repair: In client_boundary_case of both probes, accept a mask sample only when /proc shows the recorded PID alive and running exactly `sleep <unique>`, and add that client_ran condition to ok. Add a negative-control case whose stand-in publishes its PID and exits at once, expected False.
